title: Six Budget Weekend Getaways From Delhi Under ₹6,000 for September
excerpt: Monsoon shoulder season means lush landscapes, smaller crowds and pre-festive pricing on trips to Rishikesh, Jaipur, Agra, Lansdowne, Alwar and Mathura-Vrindavan.
body:
• September's monsoon shoulder season offers lush landscapes, smaller crowds and pre-festive pricing across northern India
  • All six destinations — Rishikesh, Jaipur, Agra, Lansdowne, Alwar and Mathura-Vrindavan — can be done under ₹6,000 per person for a weekend
  • Trains and buses from Delhi keep transport costs low, leaving more budget for food and experiences
  • Monsoon conditions mean some outdoor activities may be weather-dependent, so check locally before booking

September sits in that sweet spot between the monsoon and the festive season — the hills are still green, tourist crowds haven't materialised, and prices haven't climbed yet. For anyone based in or visiting Delhi, it is an ideal month to plan a quick weekend escape without a big spend. Here are six destinations within easy reach of the capital, each doable under ₹6,000 per person for a one-night, two-day trip.

Rishikesh: Hills, Ganga and Adventure

The perennial weekend favourite for Delhi residents, Rishikesh offers mountain views, riverside walks, yoga centres and enough adventure activities to fill a weekend. Spend an afternoon wandering Tapovan, sit by the Ganga, visit the ghats and catch the evening aarti. River rafting is another popular draw, though September availability depends on water levels and should be checked locally. Budget guesthouses and local eateries keep a one-night trip well within ₹6,000, and the monsoon greenery in the surrounding landscape is a bonus.

Jaipur: Royal Without the Royal Price Tag

"Budget guesthouses and local eateries keep a one-night trip well within ₹6,000, and the monsoon greenery in the surrounding landscape is a bonus."

The Pink City packs forts, palaces, colourful markets and excellent Rajasthani food into one of northern India's most photogenic destinations. Start with Hawa Mahal, explore Amber Fort and City Palace, and leave time for the old city's bazaars — especially if textiles, jewellery and handicrafts are your weakness. September can still bring warm weather and occasional rain, but train travel and budget accommodation keep costs manageable for a packed weekend.

Agra: Close, Quick, Classic

Sometimes the best getaway is the one where you spend minimal time in transit. Agra is close enough for a comfortable day trip from Delhi but works better as an overnight. Visit the Taj Mahal early, explore Agra Fort, catch Mehtab Bagh for sunset views, and leave room in the itinerary for petha and Mughlai cuisine. Inexpensive train connections and plenty of budget accommodation make it one of the most affordable weekend options from the capital.

Lansdowne: Silence and Pine Forests

For those craving quiet over activity, Lansdowne delivers. This small cantonment town in the Uttarakhand hills is surrounded by pine forests and offers little beyond walking, chai and breathing cleaner air — which is exactly the point. Visit Bhulla Lake, head to Tip N Top for panoramic views, and embrace the slower pace. September's post-monsoon greenery makes the landscape especially lush, though rain gear is essential. Simple guesthouses keep the budget well under ₹6,000.

Alwar: Rajasthan Without the Crowds

If Jaipur feels too well-trodden, Alwar offers forts, palaces, lakes and history without the tourist density. Explore Bala Quila, visit the City Palace and spend time at Siliserh Lake. Sariska Tiger Reserve is nearby for wildlife enthusiasts, though a safari needs separate budgeting. The short distance from Delhi keeps transport costs minimal, and post-monsoon greenery adds charm to the Rajasthani landscape.

Mathura-Vrindavan: A Cultural Quick Hit

For a weekend heavy on culture and light on logistics, combine Mathura and Vrindavan. The two towns are close enough to cover together — visit Krishna Janmabhoomi in Mathura, explore the temples and ghats of Vrindavan, and catch Prem Mandir in the evening light. The journey from Delhi is short, stays are affordable, and local transport keeps costs well below ₹6,000 per person.

Tips for NRIs Visiting Delhi

For diaspora visitors spending time with family in Delhi, any of these trips offers a manageable weekend break without complex planning. Book trains in advance through the IRCTC app, carry waterproof layers for monsoon conditions, and check activity availability locally — some adventure sports and wildlife safaris operate on reduced schedules in September. The festive season crowds arrive from October onward, making September one of the last windows for quieter, budget-friendly travel.
